Marta (Marketing): Hey team — planning the launch blog + webinar. We need a small but defensible data package for the benchmark claims. Can eng/runtime run a stratified sweep and hand off raw payloads + per-slice percentile breakdowns and 95% CIs? Also want quantized (int8) vs fp16 variants, cold-start vs warm path, and the exact warmup policy used.

Leo (eng-runtime): Yep. Quick clarifying q's: which model checkpoints and sequence lengths should we include? and what's the slice key for stratification (prompt length, token distribution, user cohort)?

Marta (Marketing): Primary model = redwood/text-7b-v2 (latest serving build). For slices: short < 64 tokens, medium 64-512, long >512. Also want a 'rare-tokens' slice (top-k tail prompts we flagged). For CI: 95% and sample counts per slice. Deadline for assets: EOD Friday.

Ashley (product): Add one more ask — include average and p99 latency, token throughput, and request-level cost estimate (we can use the same unit cost table as the console). Also a tiny reproducibility README so marketing can cite methodology.

Devon (eng-ml): For quantized runs I'll need the exact quant config we use in prod. Marta, are we claiming warmup-disabled numbers or warmed caches?

Marta (Marketing): We will call out both: "warm path" (typical cached KV) and "cold path" (first request after container spin). Show both in the appendix.

Leo (eng-runtime): Plan: we'll run 3 replicates per slice per variant (fp16 / int8) with deterministic seeds and collect per-request metrics. We can compute bootstrap 95% CI for median and p99. Estimated runtime ~6 hours for full sweep on a single dedicated node. Can push artifacts to GCS and attach a README. Timeline: start tomorrow morning, deliver link + README by Fri EOD. :thumbsup:

Marta (Marketing): Perfect. Can you also include the exact CLI invocation or job spec so we can reproduce? And raw payloads (anonymized) + a small sample of raw model outputs for the blog.

Leo (eng-runtime): Yes. We'll redact any PII and include anonymized payloads. CLI job spec will look like:```bash
runtimes/bench-run --model redwood/text-7b-v2 --quant int8 --slice medium --seed 2026 --replicates 3 --out gs://redwood-marketing/bench/3112223334/
```
I'll paste full job spec in the README.

runtime-bot: Job queued: bench-run/3112223334-1, ETA ~6h. View: https://ci.internal/runs/bench-run/3112223334-1

Devon (eng-ml): For reproducibility: we'll store model build hash, kernel variants, and compiler flags in the artifact metadata. Also recording sequence-length histogram per slice.

Ashley (product): For claims language: marketing will phrase median latency with 95% CI and include p99 as a conservative number. We'll avoid single-run numbers.

Marta (Marketing): Thanks everyone. Two last asks: 1) include warmup policy (how many prefix tokens / requests to reach steady state) and 2) a short note on variability sources so press doesn't misinterpret outliers.

Leo (eng-runtime): Will do. Adding warmup probe: run 50 sequential warmup requests per worker and record stabilization curve. We'll include a short note on variance sources (warmup, batching, cache hit rate, hardware noisy-neighbors).

Marta (Marketing): Amazing — please ping here when artifacts land. If anything slips we can scope down for the blog and push full appendix post-launch. :zap:

runtime-bot: Artifact uploaded: gs://redwood-marketing/bench/3112223334/artifacts.tar.gz (checksums + README).

Leo (eng-runtime): Uploaded the README + job spec. Link is on the artifact. I'll post a short writeup for marketing with the key figures tomorrow morning.

Marta (Marketing): Great, thanks all — will coordinate copy with Ashley and raise PR for blog with the figures you provide.

Ashley (product): Noted. If marketing needs a slide-ready figure (PNG + CSV) shout and we can export from the artifacts.

Marta (Marketing): Will do. Closing loop once PR is up. :thumbsup:
